messages:
maya: FYI CI on main showed a sporadic failure in runtime retry unit tests this morning. Noticed flaky failure in `tests/retry_smoke` on shard 7 (1 fail out of ~40 runs).

liam: can you paste the failing shard log / stack? was it an assertion or timeout?

maya: assertion in test harness: `expected event order [A,B] got [B,A]`
Attached the tail of the log:
```
[ RUN      ] retry_smoke
E runtime/tests/retry_smoke.cc:142: order mismatch: expected A before B
Stack: 
  at retry_backoff.cc:87
  at test_runner.cc:213
```

ci-bot: rerun requested by maya — starting rerun (10 attempts) on shard 7. Job: CI-2965004321-rerun

jess: i've seen order flips like this before when the background timer jitter overlaps test scheduling. could be nondeterministic scheduling or test relying on wall-clock timing. does the test use `std::chrono::steady_clock` vs system clock?

maya: good call. test uses a real-timer + a small sleep for ordering. local quick stress: `bazel test //runtime/tests:retry_smoke --runs_per_test=50` produced 2 failures in 50.

arturo: can you try forcing deterministic timing in the test harness? there is a fake-clock flag we sometimes use: `--test_env=FAKE_CLOCK=1` or define `-DTEST_FAKE_CLOCK` at compile time.

maya: starting a local run with FAKE_CLOCK=1. also sent a small patch to add a trace log around the ordering check so we can see timestamps if it reappears.

ci-bot: rerun complete — 1/10 attempts failed. Marked flaky: true. See CI job CI-2965004321-rerun (link).

liam: since it's reproducible locally (albeit rarely), i'd prefer a targeted bisect rather than disabling. can we add a quick bisect script to narrow to commit range that introduced timing behavior?

jess: ack. quick triage ideas: 1) run on a single-core pinned worker to reduce scheduling nondeterminism, 2) enable fake clock and re-run longer stress, 3) add a tiny backoff in test assertion to tolerate ordering if it's not semantically important.

maya: pinned single-core run done: `bazel test ... --test_env=GOMAXPROCS=1` -> passed 100/100. With FAKE_CLOCK it passed 500/500 locally. So looks like scheduling on contended hosts triggers the flip.

arturo: sounds like an infra-sensitive flake. i'll queue a CI bisect across the recent scheduler patches and run on the same worker class that saw failures. will update here when bisect results land (ETA tomorrow morning).

jess: small follow-up: if bisect points to scheduler changes, we should add a test harness improvement (use fake-clock by default for timing-sensitive tests) and add a CI matrix entry that runs these tests on contended workers occasionally.

maya: filed a PR with the trace logs + opt-in fake-clock for the test: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pulls/4321 (WIP). Adding notes for reviewers to avoid flipping on main until bisect finishes.

liam: thanks — adding `oncall` to FYI in case we need to roll back any infra rollouts.

maya: thanks all, will follow up after the bisect. :thumbsup:
